title: Hearts of Palm Salad
subtitle: with spinach, farro and quinoa
menu_blurb: Spinach, roasted asparagus, hearts of palm, tomatoes and avocado over toasted farro and quinoa, with a simple lemon and olive oil dressing.
intro: An incredibly flavorful salad with surprising ingredients that will exceed all expectations. Every time I make this salad, I get asked for the recipe.
origin: Hearts of palm salads trace back to Central America, South America, and Southeast Asia, where Indigenous communities have harvested the tender inner cores of native palms for thousands of years. Civilizations like the Maya relied on wild palms such as açaí, peach palm, and palmetto, eating the soft white inner bud raw or boiled, often tossed with other native greens. In Florida, Native Americans and early settlers harvested sabal palms for a version known as “swamp cabbage” salad.

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Spinach, avocado, hearts of palm, and tomatoes

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A baking sheet, a pot, and a large serving bowl

items.name: Hearts of palm, sliced into ½ inch pieces

steps.title: Cook the grains
instructions: Toast the quinoa and farro, then add the water with a sprinkle of salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Let cool.

steps.title: Roast the asparagus
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Spray the asparagus lightly with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Roast until lightly crispy. Once cooled, cut into thirds.

steps.title: Cut the vegetables
instructions: Cube the avocado and sprinkle it with lemon juice.
Roughly chop the spinach, halve the cherry tomatoes, and slice the hearts of palm into ½ inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
instructions: Whisk the olive oil with the juice of 1 lemon and 1 tsp salt. Taste and add more as needed.

steps.title: Bring it together
instructions: Add the spinach to a large bowl, then the asparagus, hearts of palm, and tomatoes.
Add the cooled grains and top with the avocado.
Toss with the dressing, then taste and add more salt, lemon, or olive oil as needed.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more grains if you want a less leafy salad.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keep anything you won’t serve right away separate, and add the dressing only when ready to serve.

notebook.question: What are hearts of palm, and are they good for you?
answer: A white, crunchy vegetable harvested from the inner core of certain palm trees, mostly coconut, açaí, and peach palms grown in Central and South America.
They are exceptionally good for you, packing essential nutrients into very few calories.

notebook.question: What is farro, and is it good for you?
answer: Farro is a nutty, chewy ancient whole grain, a type of wheat that has been a staple of Mediterranean and Italian cooking for thousands of years.
It is a nutrient-dense whole grain with far more benefits than refined grains like white rice or standard pasta.

notebook.question: What is quinoa, and is it good for you?
answer: Quinoa is a seed cooked and eaten like a grain, related to spinach and beets rather than true grains. It is naturally gluten-free and a complete protein, with all nine essential amino acids.
Its rare combination of complete protein, fiber, and minerals makes it a true functional superfood.
